article.articleHeadline: Hingga September 2026, DKI Jakarta Vaksinasi 31.390 Hewan Penular Rabies
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: As of September 2026, DKI Jakarta vaccinated 31,390 rabies-transmitting animals.
article.articleSummary: As of September 2026, DKI Jakarta vaccinated 31,390 rabies-transmitting animals (cats, dogs, monkeys, and civets) out of a target of 49,286, reaching 63.7% coverage. About 17,896 animals remain to reach the target. The vaccination drive is a core rabies control and prevention effort designed to stop transmission to humans. Vaccination, along with responsible pet ownership, regular animal health checks, and adherence to vaccination schedules, is emphasized as essential support. The update reflects ongoing public health measures to reduce rabies risk in Jakarta, with data reported by Bisnis.com. Progress toward the target underscores continued efforts to mitigate rabies spread among residents and animals.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: President of the European Medical Association: China's warnings about the plague are a preventive measure to avoid COVID-19 mistakes.
article.articleSummary: Dr. Fouad Aouda, president of the European–Middle Eastern Medical Association, says China's plague warnings are preventive measures to avoid COVID-19 missteps. Plague has three forms—bubonic, pneumonic, and septicemic—with pneumonic the most dangerous and bubonic accounting for 80–90% of cases. Globally, reported plague cases exceed 2,300 annually, though actual figures may be higher due to underreporting to the WHO. Pneumonic plague attacks the lungs and can spread via respiratory droplets, necessitating rapid treatment; official statistics should be publicly disclosed. China has tightened controls along its northeast border with Russia and issued precautionary alerts in Inner Mongolia after a death suspected of plague in Siberia.

triage.notes: 記事は専門家の見解を伝える論評記事であり、具体的な症例数や公式統計は示されていない。シベリアでの疑いの死亡例と内モンゴルでの警戒発令、ロシアとの国境管理強化が報じられているが、ロシアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。続報での正式な症例確認情報の有無を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Már több mint négyezer halottja van a kongói ebolajárványnak - Kenyában is megjelent a vírus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Congolese Ebola outbreak has already claimed more than four thousand lives — the virus has also appeared in Kenya.
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak driven by Bundibugyo virus: 8,978 confirmed cases and 4,336 deaths reported by WHO as of October 10, 2026. Kenya reports one imported fatal case from DRC via Uganda; no further confirmed cases after testing 293 samples by Oct 12; contacts under observation. WHO provided about $70,000 in health supplies to Kenya, including PPE, face shields, test kits and safe specimen transport. In Europe, risk remains very low; a health worker infected in Congo was evacuated to the Netherlands, marking the fourth imported case on the continent. No licensed vaccine or targeted treatment exists for Bundibugyo virus; control relies on rapid case identification, isolation, supportive care, and thorough contact tracing; many deaths occur outside treatment facilities, signaling delays in care. The situation remains severe and not yet resolved, with variation by region.

article.articleHeadline: 三医话健康：儿童易感的手足口病
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Three Doctors Talk Health: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease in Children
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) is an acute febrile exanthem caused by enteroviruses, a common infection in China. Children under 3 are most susceptible. The principal pathogens are Enterovirus 71 (EV71) and Coxsackievirus A16. Patients and asymptomatic carriers are contagious, transmitted mainly via the fecal–oral route, and also through contact with respiratory secretions, vesicle fluid, or contaminated objects. Symptoms include fever and vesicular lesions on hands, feet, and oral mucosa, often with cough, rhinorrhea, and poor appetite. Most cases are mild, but some progress to severe. Red flags include persistent high fever, irritability or vomiting, lethargy, rapid breathing or pulse, cold sweat, cold extremities, poor peripheral perfusion, hypertension, hyperglycemia, and elevated white blood cell and platelet counts. Prevention hinges on early recognition and isolation. An inactivated EV71 vaccine reduces risk; recommended for susceptible infants aged 6 months and older, ideally completed before 12 months. Emphasize handwashing, ventilation, disinfection, and avoiding contact with patients and contaminated items.

article.articleHeadline: ArkBio Announces FDA Clearance to Initiate Phase II Trial of AK0406 for Influenza Prevention
article.articleSummary: FDA cleared ArkBio's IND for AK0406, a long-acting antiviral-Fc conjugate (AFC), enabling a Phase II influenza-prevention trial in U.S. adults during a seasonal flu period. AK0406 links potent small-molecule antivirals to an antibody Fc to combine direct antiviral activity with Fc-mediated immune clearance. In preclinical studies, it showed broad activity against influenza A and B, with optimized pharmacokinetics and scalable GMP manufacturing. The U.S. Phase II will be multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, assessing influenza prevention with safety, tolerability, PK and immunogenicity as secondary objectives. The trial follows Australia’s Phase I (enrollment completed July 2026) and China’s NMPA IND clearance (Aug 2026). CDC’s 2025-2026 US season reported at least 32 million illnesses, 380,000 hospitalizations and 24,000 deaths. ArkBio seeks parallel US-China development to address waning vaccine protection in high-risk populations.

article.articleHeadline: China Warns of Plague Risk Near Russian Border
article.articleSummary: China warns of plague risk near the Russian border after a Siberian incident in Irkutsk Oblast. A 28-year-old laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov died from sudden and severe pneumonia; authorities suspect a plague link. Russian health authorities have quarantined hundreds of contacts in the Shelekhov district to prevent spread. In Heilongjiang, northeastern China, border cities such as Fuyuan have tightened health screenings and urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel to the affected region and contact with wild animals, particularly marmots. August 2026 saw a joint emergency-response drill in Fuyuan between China and Russia on imported cases, reflecting heightened preparedness. Russian authorities launched a criminal investigation into potential health and safety violations at the institute; initial tests found no microorganisms connected to the worker’s daily work. WHO is monitoring, and the public-health risk is considered low with no confirmed community spread.

article.articleHeadline: 俄羅斯遭爆肺鼠疫！驚傳蔓延中國「封城惡夢恐重演」官方急否認　卻突發1警訊內幕超毛 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia hit by a pneumonic plague outbreak! Shocking reports that it has spread to China: "Lockdown nightmare could be repeated" Officials hurriedly deny, but a single ominous insider warning suddenly surfaces — Minshi News Network
article.articleSummary: Russia’s Irkutsk Oblast in Siberia is the site of a suspected pneumonic plague outbreak, prompting neighboring countries to watch closely. Chinese social media has circulated unverified claims of plague cases in Henan, Inner Mongolia, Shanghai, and Chongqing, with no official confirmation. Alleged reports include over 70 plague patients arriving at Inner Mongolia Medical University Affiliated Hospital, Erenhot Branch, with about 40 deaths and frontline staff reportedly infected; other cities including Hohhot, Chifeng, Tongliao, and Baotou were also mentioned. Shanghai and Chongqing rumors of bioweapons add to the panic. Russia said on October 6 that the cases were diagnosed as unknown pneumonia and that tests showed no plague; no biolab accident was reported. Hunan CDC issued plague prevention reminders; authorities emphasize surveillance and that plague remains rare and treatable, urging calm.

article.articleHeadline: Perdhaki Papua Latih 30 Kader Malaria Desa di Kota Jayapura
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Perdhaki Papua Trains 30 Village Malaria Cadres in Jayapura City
article.articleSummary: As of 13 October 2026, malaria remains a major health challenge in Jayapura City, Indonesia, with an Annual Parasite Incidence of 166.6 per 1,000 in Muara Tami and near the Heram border area. Perdhaki Papua’s GF ATMR Regio Papua trained 30 Desa Juru Malaria Desa (JMD) cadres for five days starting 12 October 2026 at Hotel Horison Ultima Entrop to conduct house-to-house malaria screening as part of the national elimination target by 2030. In Kota Jayapura, about 79,000 malaria cases were recorded from 430,000 people screened, highlighting many asymptomatic infections and poor adherence to completing treatment. Fourteen kampung show lower malaria, including Kampung Kayu Pulo. Operational funding comes from Special Autonomy (Otsus), 2026 DAK Non-Fisik, and Perdhaki transport support, with officials urging community cooperation, improved hygiene, and awareness of nighttime activity to curb transmission amid ongoing mobility challenges.

article.articleHeadline: 內蒙呼倫貝爾發出「鼠疫」防控風險警示：疫情發生率低不必恐慌
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia, issues a plague prevention and control risk warning: outbreak incidence is low, no need to panic.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-13, Hulunbuir City, Inner Mongolia, issued a plague prevention and control risk alert: outbreak incidence is low, and there have been no human plague cases since 1927, with no recent rodent epizootics detected. Nevertheless, due to historical plague foci in the area and frequent cross-border travel with Russia, authorities advised travelers who visited plague-endemic areas in Russia’s Far East to monitor health and report travel history if symptoms appear. In Irkutsk, there is international attention over the death of a plague research institute worker from pneumonia of unknown cause, though official details are unconfirmed. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and is a Class A infectious disease in China, transmitted by fleas, contact with infected animals, or respiratory droplets, with bubonic, pneumonic, and septicemic forms. It is preventable and treatable; early antibiotics and proper isolation save lives, and panic is not warranted.

article.articleHeadline: 俄羅斯遭爆肺鼠疫！驚傳蔓延中國「封城惡夢恐重演」官方急否認卻突發1警訊
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia hit by pneumonic plague! Shocking reports say it’s spreading to China, with “the lockdown nightmare could recur” — officials rush to deny, but a warning sign has suddenly emerged.
article.articleSummary: Russia's Irkutsk Oblast reports a suspected pneumonic plague outbreak, triggering regional concern as rumors spread of related cases in China, including Shanghai and Chongqing. Chinese social media claimed 70 pneumonic plague patients in Inner Mongolia and 40 deaths; similar allegations surfaced about Henan Province. Authorities in Inner Mongolia denied that hospitals had treated plague patients or that large outbreaks were occurring, and Shanghai/Chongqing rumors remained unverified. Russia stated on Oct 6 that the cases were diagnosed as undetermined pneumonia and that lab tests did not identify Yersinia pestis, rejecting a bioresearch incident. In China, Hunan Provincial CDC issued plague prevention reminders, noting Yersinia pestis is a Class A infectious disease but urging calm; China maintains plague surveillance and emergency response mechanisms. Overall, no credible evidence confirms pneumonic plague spread; online rumors require verification, officials say.

article.articleHeadline: 중러 접경지역 당국, '페스트 위험 예방' 공지 발표 [자막뉴스]
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Authorities in the China–Russia border region issue a notice on 'plague risk prevention' [Subtitled News].
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 13, 2026, Hulunbuir City, Inner Mongolia, China, issued a plague risk prevention and control notice amid reports that a researcher at a Russian plague institute died under suspicion of pneumonic plague (no lab confirmation reported). The notice, attributed to the city’s CDC, states that plague is fully preventable, controllable, and curable, advising against undue fear. It highlights the border region’s history of natural plague foci and close cross-border movement with Russia’s Far East, justifying intensified prevention and response measures. The development follows prior remarks by Chinese officials that Beijing and Moscow maintain close cooperation on epidemic prevention and control, including plague.

article.articleHeadline: Uganda starts trials for vaccine against Kenya Ebola strain
article.articleSummary: Uganda has begun phase I trials of the ChAdOx BDBV vaccine against Bundibugyo Ebola virus in Masaka City, with the first volunteers dosed on October 6. The trial, led by MRC/UVRI and LSHTM Uganda Research Unit in collaboration with the University of Oxford, aims to assess safety and the ability to elicit immune responses. The Bundibugyo strain, first identified in a 2007 outbreak in western Uganda, remains without a licensed vaccine or specific treatment. Kenya confirmed its first imported Bundibugyo virus disease case on October 6 after a Kenyan man who lived in the DRC traveled via Uganda to Nairobi; he died on October 5, prompting tracing. The Serum Institute of India has stockpiled about 620,000 doses of ChAdOx BDBV, including about 3,000 for Uganda, funded by CEPI. Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) is not approved for Bundibugyo except under research protocols per WHO.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダ、ケニアのエボラ株に対するワクチン治験を開始
triage.triage_reason: ケニアでBundibugyo型エボラウイルスの輸入症例が発生し死亡者も出ており、国境を越えた感染拡大の可能性があるためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 本イベントの主体はケニアでの輸入エボラ症例とウガンダでのワクチン治験であり、いずれも対象国リストに含まれない。DRCは感染者の過去の居住地として言及されているのみで発生国ではなく、インドはワクチン製造・備蓄国としての言及のみであるため、いずれもverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Chinese Border City Issues Plague Alert for Travelers From Russia's Far East
article.articleSummary: Plague risk alert issued by the Hulunbuir Center for Disease Control and Prevention in Inner Mongolia, China, urging travelers from plague-endemic areas of Russia’s Far East to monitor health and seek prompt care if symptoms develop. The advisory, reported by Inner Mongolia Radio and Television, requires incoming travelers to disclose travel history to medical staff when seeking treatment for suspected symptoms. The alert follows the death of a researcher at a Russian infectious-disease institute and underscores cross-border concerns about plague exposure. Affected locations include Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia, and plague-endemic areas of Russia’s Far East; no case counts are cited. The guidance highlights the importance of travel history disclosure during medical evaluation for suspected plague symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: 中国国境都市、ロシア極東からの渡航者向けにペスト警戒を発令
triage.triage_reason: ロシア極東の感染症研究所職員の死亡を受け、中国・内モンゴル自治区フルンボイル市が越境感染リスクを懸念しペスト警戒を発令しており、国際的拡大リスクと異常性の両方が認められるためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 中国国内での確定症例数は報告されておらず、警戒はロシア極東における研究所職員の死亡を契機とした予防的な渡航者モニタリング措置である。ロシア側の詳細（死亡者の感染経路・病型等）は不明。

article.articleHeadline: 鼠疫擴散中國？網傳內蒙、河南淪陷　上海、重慶也爆病例｜壹蘋新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Is the plague spreading in China? Online rumors claim Inner Mongolia and Henan have fallen; Shanghai and Chongqing also report cases | YiPin News Network
article.articleSummary: Rumors claim pneumonic plague is spreading in China, with alleged cases in Inner Mongolia (Hulunbuir and Erenhot), Henan, Shanghai, and Chongqing. The concern follows a Siberia-based plague prevention institute reporting the death of staff from unknown pneumonia; no laboratory confirmation linking the death to plague has been provided, and the WHO has not verified a plague connection. Inner Mongolia’s disease control center issued a plague risk alert, but authorities in Hohhot, Chifeng, Tongliao, Baotou and other cities deny any plague patients or domestic transmission. Social media posts allege 70+ infections and 40+ deaths in Erenhot, alleged changes to medical records to avoid the word ‘plague,’ and outbreaks in other cities, yet no verifiable case data exists. Anonymous claims citing a P4 laboratory describe imported cases in Shanghai and Chongqing from Russia, also unsubstantiated. Authorities caution against misinformation; no confirmed outbreaks or laboratory-confirmed cases are reported.

article.articleSummary: Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia issues a plague risk warning after a Russian laboratory death draws attention. Some reports mention a broken vial; her mother disputes this. A possible plague link in Buryatia near the Russia–Mongolia border is denied by its leader, who still notes plague relevance. article.articleHeadline: Las muertes por cólera alcanzaron en 2025 su cifra más alta desde 1999, según balance de la OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cholera deaths in 2025 reached their highest toll since 1999, according to the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Cholera deaths in 2025 reached their highest toll since 1999, with 451,499 cases and 7,870 deaths reported by the WHO across 47 countries. Seven countries—Angola, Bangladesh, Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Sudan, South Sudan, and Yemen—accounted for about 90% of cases and deaths. In Africa, cholera cases rose 34% and deaths 58% versus 2024. Vibrio cholerae infection, transmitted via contaminated water or food, causes acute watery diarrhea and dehydration; mortality is low with timely rehydration, but more than one in five 2025 deaths occurred outside health facilities, and facility-based case fatality exceeded 1% in 12 countries. Vaccination momentum grew: global oral cholera vaccine production rose from ~30 million doses in 2022 to ~80 million in 2025, with 71 million doses approved for affected countries and 20 million for preventive use resumed early 2026. Jan–Aug 2026 reported 275,284 cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries, versus 480,199 cases and 6,180 deaths in the same period of 2025; August 2026 alone had 41,915 cases and 348 deaths in 17 countries.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russian "plague researcher" dies of unknown pneumonia! Inner Mongolia CDC: outbreak risk is low, but frequent cross-border travel requires vigilance.
article.articleSummary: On 2 October, a researcher at Russia’s Plague Control Research Institute died of unknown pneumonia; the death's cause is not yet confirmed. Plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, transmits via flea bites, direct contact with infected animals, or respiratory droplets, and presents as bubonic, pneumonic, or septicemic forms. Early detection, isolation, and antibiotic treatment are effective; current risk remains low, with vigilant monitoring advised.

article.articleHeadline: Hidden Scourge: Genital Tuberculosis Strikes Young Women and Evades
article.articleSummary: In Shenzhen, China, a five-year retrospective study at a large tertiary hospital (Jan 2018–Dec 2022) of 5,123 female TB patients identified 59 genital tuberculosis (FGTB) cases. FGTB patients were significantly younger than other female TB patients (P<0.001), with 27 of 59 aged 20–29. Genital TB accounted for about 1.36–2.39% of extrapulmonary TB, peaking in 2021; abdominal TB was most common, including tuberculous peritonitis (19, 32.2%) and intestinal TB (8, 13.56%). Clinically, gynecologic/abdominal symptoms dominated over pulmonary signs: abnormal uterine bleeding (15/59, 25.4%), abdominal pain (~39%), distension (20%), and weight loss (12%). Ultrasound abnormalities were common: ovarian changes (31.1% of 45), pelvic effusion (22.2%), and endometrial abnormalities (11.1%). Histopathology was most reliable: 32/35 (91.4%) of tissue samples were positive for caseating granulomas; molecular tests showed inconsistent yields due to paucibacillary samples, and acid-fast staining had limited utility.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Antimicrobial peptide market to reach $10.4 billion by 2030 — A new weapon to combat antibiotic-resistant infections — CNET Japan
article.articleSummary: Antimicrobial peptide (AMP) market is projected to grow from $7.03 billion in 2025 to $10.4 billion by 2030 (CAGR 8.1%), with 2026 at about $7.62 billion (CAGR 8.4%). AMP, short proteins that disrupt pathogen membranes, are being developed from plant, bacterial, animal, and insect sources for broad-spectrum uses against bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites. Driven by antimicrobial resistance and limits of traditional therapies, AMP therapeutics span infection, antiviral, and antifungal indications, plus agricultural and veterinary applications. In England, HIV diagnoses rose 15% from 2022 (2,451) to 2023 (2,810). Market segments include source (plant, bacteria, animal, insect), disease targets (pneumonia, hepatitis, bacterial infections, HIV), administration (topical, subcutaneous, intravenous), and channels (hospitals, research institutes, clinics, pharmacies). Major players include WuXi AppTec, Sigma-Aldrich, Ipsen, Novozymes, GenScript; North America leads 2025 market, Asia-Pacific grows fastest.

article.articleHeadline: 鼠疫疑雲》俄方解除隔離　疾管署：台灣備有檢驗與抗生素
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Plague Mystery: Russia Lifts Quarantine; Taiwan CDC Says It Has Testing and Antibiotics on Hand
article.articleSummary: A plague-related death in Russia’s Irkutsk Oblast raised questions about possible pneumonic plague. An employee of a plague-control research institute died of severe pneumonia; the exact cause is not yet confirmed, and WHO is still investigating. By Oct 13, 2026, Russia reported no recent plague cases and no high-threat pathogens among contacts; about 200 people linked to the case were quarantined or under medical observation since Oct 2, and roughly 5,000 tests found no related high-threat pathogens; isolation was lifted Oct 8. The event spurred cross-border vigilance: Manzhouli, Inner Mongolia, held a risk assessment on Oct 8 and Hulunbuir issued Oct 10 guidance for people from Russia’s Far East plague areas. In China, Hunan and Guangdong released plague prevention notices; Hunan says no natural foci and low daily risk. WHO notes no evidence of sustained transmission, while Russia denies a recent plague presence or lab incident. Taiwan’s CDC asserts testing capacity and antibiotics on hand, with no plague since 1953, ongoing border fever screening and a ready diagnostic/ treatment network. Globally, WHO data (2019–2025) show 3,860 suspected and 2,646 confirmed cases, 423 deaths, predominantly in Congo and Madagascar; neighboring China and Mongolia reported 19 and 17 confirmed cases, respectively.

article.articleHeadline: India's Mycetoma Burden Calls For One Health Lens - Analysis
article.articleSummary: India's Mycetoma (Madura Foot) remains underreported with minimal national surveillance, despite NOHM's push to integrate human, animal, and environmental health. In Kolkata labs, two distinct soil fungi caused mycetoma in a single 60-year-old farmer who first injured his foot by a cow's hoof, then developed a buttock lesion after a thorn prick three years later. Rajasthan's Baburam Bishnoi—barefoot for decades—developed progressive lower-limb disease with yearly rainy-season flares, in Khetasar village. Mycetoma arises from actinomycetoma bacteria or eumycetoma fungi entering via minor trauma; the lower limb affected in 77% of cases; >80 causative organisms, with 69 fungal species. In 2022, eumycetoma fungi were added to WHO's fungal priority list. Diagnosis shows swelling, draining sinuses, grainy discharge; pain mounts. A One Health approach, integrating soil, thorn vegetation, and animal dung ecology, is urged; Gujarat’s leptospirosis model is cited as evidence for coordinated action.

article.articleHeadline: Sốt, mất khứu giác, vị giác, có người hỏi 'có phải do COVID không?'
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fever, loss of smell and taste; some people ask, 'Could it be COVID?'
article.articleSummary: Loss of smell and taste is not specific to COVID-19. While anosmia was common during earlier COVID waves (Alpha, Delta), Omicron reduced its frequency; nonetheless, smell/taste loss can accompany other respiratory infections. In Hanoi, Oct 2–9, 2026, seven COVID-19 cases were reported in seven wards, with a cumulative 1,667 cases in 122 wards since the start of 2026 and no deaths; there is no observed surge in COVID-19, while influenza activity has risen. The National Institute notes that most flu cases are mild, but influenza A can cause pneumonia and respiratory failure, especially in older adults and those with chronic diseases. For example, a 72-year-old man with hypertension and prior stroke developed severe influenza A pneumonia requiring intensive care and noninvasive ventilation; another COPD patient deteriorated to respiratory failure. Fever or cough alone cannot distinguish COVID-19 from influenza; monitor progression and seek care for respiratory distress.

article.articleHeadline: 中山检查组走进东区社区和幼儿园 推进蚊媒传染病防控
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Zhongshan inspection team visits Eastern District communities and kindergartens to promote the prevention and control of mosquito-borne infectious diseases.
article.articleSummary: On October 12, 2026, Zhongshan Vice Mayor Chen Huidong led an inspection team to the Eastern District to promote prevention and control of mosquito-borne infectious diseases. They visited Qiwan and Xin'ao Ling communities to assess residential environment remediation, anti-mosquito facilities, and breeding-site cleanup, and they checked health monitoring and morning/afternoon screening in kindergartens. The team urged heightened awareness and sustained effort, stressing the current peak of mosquito-borne disease activity. They called for scientifically based, precise disinfection per guidelines, conducted during peak mosquito activity times, with no missed areas and with vector density kept below safe thresholds. Focus on high-risk groups and strengthened health monitoring and early warning/response were emphasized. Schools and daycare centers must enforce morning/afternoon checks and illness-absence tracking to enable early detection and prevent spread. The Eastern District Epidemic Command later met to implement municipal directives and tighten prevention networks to avoid a large-scale outbreak.

A China–Russia cross-border infectious-disease drill on 24–27 Aug in Fuyuan, Heilongjiang addressed imported plague, with the Irkutsk institute’s director involved, fueling online speculation about risk. Thai mystic Mor Plai’s 2025 forecast for 2026 mentioned plague and other ancient diseases, but the article notes only rumors and precaution, with no verified outbreak reported.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペスト発生疑惑！ タイの霊媒師がかつて警告した「死者が木の葉のように落ちる」...6大予言を一挙紹介
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクの感染症研究所職員が原因不明の肺炎で死亡したが、ペスト（鼠疫）としての確定診断は未発表であり、噂・予言の域を出ない。研究所事故という異常性はあるため続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は噂・予言であり、実際の感染発生地はロシア（対象国リスト外）。中国（黒竜江省）は8月の越境感染症演習の文脈で言及されたのみで、実際の患者発生ではない。タイも予言者の発言のみで実際の発生地ではないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。ラボでの病原体漏洩事故と原因不明肺炎による死亡という異常性から、公式発表を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: 黑死病攻入上海、重慶？中俄邊境引爆逃亡潮　專家警告：真相恐怕更恐怖
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Black Death Invades Shanghai and Chongqing? A Mass Exodus Triggered at the China-Russia Border; Experts Warn: The Truth May Be Even More Terrifying.
article.articleSummary: Sept 29–Oct 2, 2026: In Irkutsk, Russia, Darya Shipilova, 28, a technician at the Irkutsk Plague Research Institute, died after severe pneumonia; Russia quarantined about 20 close contacts. Authorities later attributed death to unknown pneumonia, not plague, while experts warn inconsistent explanations and mass isolation may mask a larger outbreak. Mongolia activated emergency health surveillance along a 3,000-km Russia–China border; Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan issued entry alerts. Across China, rumors allege a plague surge reaching Inner Mongolia (Erenhot), Henan, Shanghai, and Chongqing; posts claim over 70 plague patients at Inner Mongolia Medical University Affiliated Hospital in Erenhot, with about 40 deaths and infections among staff. Chinese authorities deny domestic plague cases; Inner Mongolia officials say no plague patients have been treated and no confirmed domestic cases exist. The situation remains under international scrutiny.

triage.headline_ja: 黒死病が上海・重慶に侵入？中露国境で脱出劇、専門家警告「真相はもっと恐ろしいかもしれない」
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクのペスト研究所職員の死亡を契機に、モンゴル・カザフスタン・ウズベキスタン・キルギスが国境警戒や入国警戒を発令するなど国際的な対応が見られ、中国国内でもペスト拡大の噂が広範に拡散している。中国当局は否定しているが、複数国にまたがる緊張と情報の不整合があり、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 確定症例が報告されたのはロシア（対象国リスト外）。中国国内（上海、重慶、内モンゴル、河南）での感染拡大は噂ベースであり、中国当局は公式に否定している。情報の信頼性に注意が必要だが、複数国の警戒対応という社会的・政治的関心の高まりからPICKUPと判定。続報で中国当局の公式発表や検査結果を確認する必要あり。

article.articleHeadline: 我国地方首次发布针对俄罗斯鼠疫防控风险提示
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Local authorities in China issue first risk warning for Russian plague prevention and control.
article.articleSummary: On Oct 11, Hulunbuir City Center for Disease Control and Prevention in Inner Mongolia issued China’s first local risk alert for Russian plague prevention, urging people coming from Russia’s Far East plague-origin regions to monitor health and report travel history if symptoms arise. The trigger is the death of a 28-year-old female researcher at the Irkutsk-Siberia and Far East Anti-Plague Research Institute from an undiagnosed pneumonia; the institute handles high-risk pathogens including Yersinia pestis (plague). Russian officials offered inconsistent explanations and withheld diagnostic data, prompting the WHO to request more information. Historical parallels to Chernobyl and Sverdlovsk are cited to stress transparency and risk assessment. Manzhouli, Heilongjiang, encompasses a 150 sq km plague focus; the 1910 outbreak originated there and spread to Harbin via the Trans-Manchurian Railway, linked to marmot hunting in Russia. Modern cross-border movement exceeds 3 million annually, with over 750,000 Russian travelers entering Manzhouli, reinforcing border-to-inland surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: 中国地方当局、ロシアのペスト予防に関する初の危険性警告を発令
triage.triage_reason: ロシアの研究所職員が原因不明の肺炎（ペスト疑い）で死亡し、情報開示が不透明なままWHOが追加情報を要求。中国内モンゴルが初の越境リスク警告を発令し、年間300万人超の越境移動を背景に国際的拡大リスクが懸念される。
triage.notes: 原因不明の死亡例がロシアで発生し、同国側の情報開示が不透明なためWHOが照会中。中国は越境リスクを懸念し内モンゴル（満洲里）で警戒を強化。ロシアは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsには中国のみを計上。続報でロシア側の診断結果（ペスト確定の有無）を要確認。

article.articleHeadline: Mumbai News: जे. जे. वसतिगृहात २१ वर्षीय विद्यार्थ्याचा मृत्यू, अस्वच्छतेमुळे साथीच्या आजारांची ९० जणांना लागण
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mumbai News: A 21-year-old student's death at JJ Hostel; 90 people contract infectious diseases due to unsanitary conditions.
article.articleSummary: 21-year-old Gajanan Jamge, a third-semester BSc Nursing student at the JJ Group of Hospitals nursing college in Mumbai, died after malaria diagnosed on admission; his death was declared on Saturday night. Autopsy indicated severe malaria causing multi-organ failure, including acute kidney injury and brain hemorrhage. The incident highlighted filthy hostel conditions, with contaminated water, unclean toilets, stagnant water, and mosquito breeding cited as factors. Officials said the hostel's water tank had not been cleaned in four years; sanitation lapses included poorly cleaned washrooms, open drainage from canteen, and storage of biomedical waste. About 90 students—roughly 40+ BSc Nursing and over 50 undergraduate/postgraduate students—were afflicted with dengue, malaria, and typhoid and were undergoing treatment in hospitals. Students allege neglect and call for immediate remedial action.

triage.headline_ja: ムンバイニュース：JJ寮で21歳の学生が死亡、不衛生な環境により90人が感染症に罹患
triage.triage_reason: 単一施設内で90名規模の複数感染症（マラリア・デング・腸チフス）集団発生と死亡例が確認され、不衛生な環境要因（汚染水・蚊の発生）が継続的曝露リスクを示しており、メディア報道による社会的関心も高いため、フルリスク評価での確認が望ましい。
triage.notes: ムンバイの看護学生寮という単一施設内での衛生管理不備に起因する局所的アウトブレイク。国際的拡大リスクは低いが、死亡例・重症例の発生、メディア報道の高まりから国内公衆衛生対応として注視が必要。衛生状態改善（給水タンク清掃等）の是正措置の進展を確認すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Beni: 18 recovered patients discharged in succession over a six-day period - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola in Beni, Nord-Kivu, DR Congo: Eighteen recovered patients were discharged from two Ebola treatment centers in Beni over Oct 5-11, 2026. Dr. Jeremie Muhindo, medical director of the Beni General Reference Hospital, confirmed that four of the discharged patients were healthcare workers (one doctor, three nurses). Authorities urge continued trust in healthcare teams and prompt medical attention for symptoms to enable investigation and isolation if confirmed. The case fatality rate in the Beni health zone has fallen from 50% to about 29-30% since the outbreak began, with officials aiming to push it below 15% in the coming days. The outbreak's first case was confirmed May 18, 2026. As of Oct 11, 2026, the Beni health zone has recorded 433 cases and 338 deaths, according to the provincial response coordination unit bulletin.

triage.headline_ja: ベニのエボラ出血熱:6日間で18人の回復患者が相次いで退院 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: DRC・Nord-KivuでのエボラアウトブレイクはIHR基準（重大な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク）を複数満たし、継続中の致死率約30%の深刻な状況であるためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 2026年5月18日に始まったベニ保健地区でのエボラアウトブレイクは、10月11日時点で433症例・338死亡、致死率は50%から約29-30%に低下しているが依然として深刻。医療従事者への感染も確認されており、継続的な監視と国際支援が必要と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: 俄疑爆鼠疫！中國留學生急囤口罩「幾乎買光藥店」 俄人反應曝
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Plague outbreak suspected in Russia! Chinese international students rush to stock up on masks, nearly buying out pharmacies; Russians' reactions revealed.
article.articleSummary: Russia faces a suspected plague incident after a 28-year-old researcher at a plague prevention institute in Irkutsk died on Oct 2 from severe pneumonia. The World Health Organization says the exact cause is under investigation and there are no signs of sustained human-to-human transmission at present. Mongolia has activated border health surveillance due to cross-border movement, and China's Inner Mongolia Hulunbuir CDC issued plague prevention guidance on Oct 10. In Irkutsk, Chinese international students report alarm, with many stocking up on masks—one student says pharmacies near-eliminated stock—while locals pay less attention; schools reportedly did not issue extra notices. The event underscores potential risk of pneumonic plague spread, though authorities have not confirmed transmission.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペスト発生疑い！中国人留学生がマスクを買い占め「薬局がほぼ売り切れ」、ロシア人の反応が明らかに
triage.triage_reason: ペスト予防研究所の研究者が重症肺炎で死亡し、肺ペストの疑いがあることから公衆衛生上重大かつ異常な事象であり、国境を越えた監視体制強化など国際的拡大リスクも認められるためフルリスク評価へ進めるべきと判断した。
triage.notes: 事象発生地はロシア・イルクーツク州であり対象国リストに含まれない。モンゴル・中国（内モンゴル）は国境監視や予防指導を実施しているのみで、実際の症例発生は確認されていないため verified_locations には含めなかった。

article.articleHeadline: Cao điểm bệnh tay chân miệng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Peak of hand, foot and mouth disease.
article.articleSummary: Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) in Dong Nai, Vietnam, is at a peak. Since the start of the year, the province has recorded more than 12,400 HFMD cases with 1 death. The outbreak is entering a high-transmission phase, with 500–700 weekly cases and rising hospitalizations; many children are admitted with severe illness (levels 2A–3). Transmission occurs through saliva, secretions, and contaminated objects. Early signs include rashes on hands, feet, knees, and buttocks, plus oral ulcers, fever, poor appetite, and fatigue. Parents are urged to seek medical care for warning symptoms to prevent progression; emphasize hand hygiene and cleaning of toys. Vaccination details: for 2 months–2 years, three doses (first two ~2 months apart; third ~10 months after the second); for 2–<6 years, two doses ~2 months apart. The EV71-focused HFMD vaccine is available nationwide via VNVC and should be given early, even after recovery, pending clinician screening.

triage.headline_ja: 手足口病の流行ピーク
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ドンナイ省で手足口病（HFMD）が季節的ピークを迎えているが、同国では毎年発生する既知の感染症であり、異常性や国際的拡大の証拠はない。重症例増加の兆候はあるため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: HFMDはベトナムで毎年流行する季節性感染症であり、今回の報告はドンナイ省における地域的な公衆衛生情報提供が主目的。国際的な異常性や渡航制限の懸念は確認されない。

article.articleHeadline: 不祥之兆！中國疫情升溫 河北驚現漫天烏鴉（視頻） | 河北平泉市 | 河北重症患者增多 | 染疫猝死
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ominous omen! China's outbreak heats up as Hebei experiences a sky full of crows (Video) | Pingquan, Hebei | Hebei sees an increase in severe cases | Infection-related sudden deaths.
article.articleSummary: On Oct 12, 2026, Pingquan, Hebei, China, witnessed a large flock of crows over Pingquan Square amid reports of a sharp uptick in severe COVID-19 cases in northern China. Chinese virologists say the SARS-CoV-2 variant PJ.2.1 binds ACE2 more efficiently and is driving a high transmission surge, with a notable rise in critical illness in Hebei and confirmed cases at sentinel hospitals in Shanxi, Jilin, and Liaoning. Wastewater surveillance indicated PJ.2.1 peaked in August and remains elevated in the north. A Beijing-based virologist stated sudden deaths among infected individuals have risen, with heart stoppage and vascular complications described as prominent. Nationwide, July saw 522,000 newly diagnosed COVID-19 cases, though hospital data underestimate true infections; cremation queues have formed in multiple cities, including Dalian. Official data reportedly suppressed; no details on infection sources or imported/exported cases were provided.

triage.headline_ja: 不祥の兆し！中国の疫病が過熱、河北省で空を覆うカラスの大群が出現（動画）｜河北省平泉市｜河北省で重症患者増加｜感染関連の突然死
triage.triage_reason: 中国北部でのCOVID-19新変異株PJ.2.1による重症化・突然死増加が報告されているが、情報源が政治色の強い大紀元系メディアであり、「カラスの大群」「不祥の兆し」等のセンセーショナルな表現や未検証の「公式データ隠蔽」主張を含むため信頼性に疑問があり、主流メディア・WHO等での裏付けが取れるまで経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 情報源(NTD/大紀元系)は政治的偏向が強く、センセーショナルな演出（カラスの大群、不祥の兆し）や「公式データ隠蔽」といった未検証の主張を含むため、科学的根拠・一次情報源（中国CDC、WHO等）による裏付けが必要。PJ.2.1変異株の実在性・伝播性についても公式発表やWHO分類での確認が取れていない点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Wie Deutschland medizinisches Personal im Kampf gegen Ebola schult
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How Germany trains healthcare workers in the fight against Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has reached about 9,000 infections and 4,000 deaths (case fatality ~50%), with Ituri and North Kivu as frontline regions. German specialists train local healthcare workers to treat patients safely and prevent spread; Louise Götze recently instructed roughly 30 clinicians in Entebbe, Uganda, and graduates in Kinshasa have started training others in case cases reach the capital. The program aims to build a regional pool of about 120 East African Community clinicians to propagate expertise across East Africa. About 800–1,000 patients are actively ill or in treatment across Ituri and Nord-Kivu. Berlin simulations demonstrate care workflows using PPE-light methods, including plastic walls with arm ports to reduce full protective gear use, given gear lasts only 45–60 minutes in tropical conditions. Germany has committed ~€21 million for PPE and training; Kenya and Uganda have reported cases as well.

triage.headline_ja: ドイツがエボラ対策のため医療従事者を訓練する方法
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で約9,000人感染・4,000人死亡（致死率約50%）という大規模なエボラ流行が続いており、ケニア・ウガンダへの越境感染も報告されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はドイツの医療従事者訓練プログラムが主題だが、感染拡大の実態はコンゴ民主共和国（イトゥリ、北キヴ）が中心。ケニア・ウガンダでの症例報告もあるが対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: 内蒙古呼伦贝尔发布鼠疫防控提示 科学防控勿恐慌
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia, issues plague prevention and control tips; follow scientific prevention and do not panic.
article.articleSummary: Hulunbuir City, Inner Mongolia, issued a plague prevention alert after reports about a staff member at Russia’s Irkutsk Institute of Plague Prevention and Control dying of pneumonia. No official confirmation of plague risk, but Hulunbuir has had no human plague cases since 1927, and rodent plague surveillance shows no activity; risk is considered low. The area borders Russia’s Far East, with cross-border travel, warranting vigilance. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and presents as bubonic, pneumonic, or septicemic forms. Incubation is typically 1–6 days (usually 2–3; up to 8–9). Transmission via flea bites, contact with infected animals, or respiratory droplets. Prevention includes avoiding hunting or handling wild plague reservoirs, not eating wild game, not transporting infected animals or products, wearing protective clothing outdoors, and seeking prompt medical care for fever, lymphadenopathy, cough, or weakness. Early antibiotics and isolation save lives; do not panic and follow official guidance.

triage.headline_ja: 内蒙古呼伦貝爾、ペスト予防対策の注意喚起を発表 科学的予防に努め、パニックにならないよう呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクでの職員死亡報道を受けた予防喚起であり、現地では1927年以降ヒト感染例なし、げっ歯類サーベイランスも異常なしで実際のペスト発生は未確認だが、国境を越えた往来があるため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事はロシア側での死亡報告を受けた中国・内モンゴル呼伦貝爾市の予防喚起が主題。ロシアはCEPR対象国リストに含まれないため除外。実際のペスト発生・確定症例は報告されておらず、現地当局はリスクを低いと評価している。

article.articleHeadline: Gia tăng trẻ nhập viện do virus gây viêm phổi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Increase in hospitalizations of children due to a pneumonia-causing virus.
article.articleSummary: As of 13 October 2026, Nghệ An Lung Hospital reported over 250 pediatric admissions for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in the past month, about three times higher than the same period in 2025. RSV commonly causes bronchiolitis, pneumonia, and wheeze, with severe illness in newborns, preterm infants, and children under 2 or with underlying conditions. Transmission occurs via droplets and contaminated surfaces; prevention includes frequent handwashing, cleaning toys and touched surfaces, avoiding close contact with symptomatic individuals, and limiting time in crowded places. Parents should monitor for cough, runny nose, fever, or wheeze and seek care promptly if rapid breathing, chest indrawing, cyanosis, lethargy, or poor feeding occur. The report also notes Adenovirus as a common pediatric respiratory pathogen that can progress to pneumonia and, without timely treatment, cause respiratory failure or long-term lung damage.

triage.headline_ja: 肺炎を引き起こすウイルスによる小児入院の増加
triage.triage_reason: RSVによる小児入院が前年同期比約3倍に増加しているが、季節性呼吸器感染症の範囲内であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。地域的な医療負荷として経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: RSVは既知の季節性病原体であり、入院者数増加は例年の流行パターンの範囲内である可能性が高いが、前年比3倍という増加幅は注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Maharashtra Is Sizzling In October. Now, Water Shortages, Drought And Dengue Add To The Worry
article.articleSummary: Maharashtra endures record October heat across the Konkan coast with Mumbai recording 38.2°C on October 12, the hottest October day since 2015; Ratnagiri and Harnai port each set new October highs (Ratnagiri 38.0–39.2°C across Oct 2–12; Harnai 38.5°C on Oct 12). The heat stems from a persistent high-pressure area and early monsoon withdrawal. Prolonged drought hits Jalna district's Kadwanchi village, damaging grape vineyards; farmers seek Rs 1 lakh per hectare aid. Pune Municipal Corporation imposes weekly Thursday water shutdowns amid a 10% state-mandated reduction and El Niño concerns; Mumbai continues water cuts through Aug 31, 2027, with demand around 4,664 MLD vs supply ~4,100 MLD and a 10% cut for all users plus 20% for industry/commercial/sports. Dengue continues to rise in Pune, with 2,391 cases recorded as September accounts for 40% of total.

triage.headline_ja: マハラシュートラ州、10月の猛暑に見舞われる。水不足、干ばつ、デング熱が懸念材料に
triage.triage_reason: プネーでデング熱症例が季節的に増加しているが、重症度や死亡者数などの詳細情報がなく、異常性も明確でないため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: 記事は主に猛暑・水不足・干ばつに焦点を当てており、デング熱は付随的な言及に留まる。プネーで2,391症例、9月が全体の40%を占めるとの記述があるが、重症度や死亡者数の情報は記載なし。季節性のデング熱増加であり、特段の異常性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death reported in Kenya as epidemic reaches 9,000 confirmed cases
article.articleSummary: Kenya confirmed its first Ebola death from a Bundibugyo infection imported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The patient, who had lived in Congo, traveled through Uganda to Kenya and died in Nairobi on Oct 5; Kenya confirmed the Bundibugyo case on Oct 6. By Oct 11, Congo’s outbreak reached about 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,339 confirmed deaths (case fatality ratio 48.2%), roughly six times the number at the same stage of West Africa’s 2014–16 epidemic. In Kenya, 122 contacts were traced, 108 in quarantine, with 293 samples tested—only one positive. In Ituri and North Kivu, 47 new positives on Oct 9 included 25 from dead bodies; 30 of the day’s 40 deaths occurred outside treatment centers. MSF notes over 60% of Ebola deaths occur in the community; test positivity fell from 20.4% to 16% between Oct 2 and Oct 9. Bas-Uélé reports Ervebo vaccine stockout (1,500 vaccinated of 13,202 target). The outbreak spans seven provinces over ~679,000 km2, with North Kivu contributing ~40% of new cases; West Africa’s 2014–16 epidemic had 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: ケニアでエボラ死亡例が報告、流行は確定症例9,000人に到達
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ由来のエボラ(ブンディブギョ)がケニアへ越境拡大し死亡例が発生、流行は9,000例・致死率48.2%に達しており、国際的拡大・深刻な公衆衛生影響・渡航制限リスクの複数のIHR基準に該当するためフルRRAへ。
triage.notes: ケニア・ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。主因となる流行はDRCで継続中であり、越境症例がケニアで確認された点が国際拡大リスクの根拠。ワクチン(Ervebo)の在庫不足も管理可能性への懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: 俄羅斯疑現鼠疫　卓榮泰：緊盯當地疫情
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia Reports Suspected Plague; Zhu Rong-tai: Closely Monitoring the Local Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Russia reports suspected plague with pneumonic form in Siberia, prompting global concern. No laboratory confirmation of the pathogen or positive samples has been reported, and the World Health Organization has not confirmed an outbreak. Pneumonic plague spreads via respiratory droplets and carries high mortality (up to ~60%), unlike bubonic or septicemic forms. Taiwan’s Premier Zhu Rong-tai says the government is closely monitoring the situation, following a two-week-ago executive meeting directive for the Ministry of Health and Welfare to report and maintain vigilance on the local outbreak. The MOH has liaised with the WHO through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to verify any deaths among Russian laboratory personnel. The Mainland Affairs Council is receiving real-time updates. Despite rumors about China, no specific cases are confirmed; Taiwan will strengthen surveillance of cross-strait Small Three Links exchanges.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペスト疑い発生、卓栄泰氏：現地の疫病情報を注視
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・シベリアでの肺ペスト疑い事例は異常性が高く、人-人感染（飛沫感染）による国際拡大リスクがあり、IHR基準の2項目以上に該当する可能性があるためフルRRAへの移行を推奨する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシア（シベリア）での肺ペスト疑い事例であり、検査確認やWHOによる公式確認は未了。台湾では政府レベルで監視強化の動きがあるが、台湾自体での症例は報告されていない。中国については噂があるものの具体的症例は未確認のため、対象国リストに含まれる中国（1814991）も実発生国としては確認できず、verified_locationsには含めなかった。ロシアおよび台湾は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: DOH reports 46% drop in leptospirosis cases
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis cases in the country show a 46% year-on-year drop, with 13,158 cases recorded in 2026 as of 7 October. The Department of Health (DOH) noted a CFR of 5.34% for the year to date. Year-to-date cases are 48% higher than the 8,910 reported in the same period in 2025, while the CFR remains below last year's 10.47%. Despite the decline, the DOH will actively monitor cases to verify that the downward trend is maintained. The report highlights ongoing transmission this year but indicates improvement in mortality relative to 2025. Data timing: as of 7 October, nationwide counts. No laboratory confirmation details or transmission sources are provided in the report.

triage.headline_ja: 保健省、レプトスピラ症症例が46%減少と報告
triage.triage_reason: 症例数は減少傾向にあり、既知の風土病に対する通常のサーベイランス報告であるため、新規性や異常性に乏しく、緊急対応の必要性は低い。
triage.notes: フィリピンの風土病であるレプトスピラ症の年次統計報告であり、致死率も前年より改善している。DOHによる通常モニタリングの範囲内。

article.articleHeadline: 俄羅斯研究員疑染肺鼠疫猝逝！嚇壞中國留學生驚慌掃光藥局口罩
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russian researcher suspected of contracting pneumonic plague dies suddenly! Chinese international students panic and empty pharmacies of masks.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague concerns erupt in Irkutsk, Russia after a 28-year-old researcher at a plague-control institute dies from severe pneumonia; death reportedly occurred on Oct 2, with the cause and specific pathogen sequencing still pending. WHO says there is no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission based on contact tracing, though the exact death cause remains under investigation. The incident has sparked anxiety among Chinese international students at Irkutsk National University, prompting postponement of gatherings and stockpiling of antibiotics, with local pharmacies reportedly selling out of masks. Russia has signaled the overall public health situation as stable and has lifted preliminary preventive measures. Border countries respond: Mongolia activates border health surveillance, while China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region’s CDC issues risk alerts urging vigilance, avoidance of wild animals, and enhanced self-monitoring to prevent cross-border spread.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアの研究員が肺ペスト感染疑いで急死！中国人留学生がパニックになり薬局のマスクを買い占める
triage.triage_reason: ペスト研究機関の研究員が肺ペスト感染疑いで死亡するという異常事態が発生し、中国・モンゴルが国境対応を強化するなど社会的関心も高まっているため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断する。
triage.notes: 実際の発症・死亡事例はロシア（イルクーツク）で発生しており、対象国リストに含まれない。中国内モンゴル自治区やモンゴルは警戒態勢の強化・国境監視を実施しているのみで、現地での症例確認は記事内に言及がないため verified_locations には含めなかった。病原体の確定診断（シークエンシング）は未完了で、WHOは持続的ヒト-ヒト感染の証拠なしとしている点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Bộ Y tế khuyến cáo 8 biện pháp phòng, chống cúm mùa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ministry of Health advises eight measures to prevent and control seasonal influenza.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-13, Vietnam's Department of Preventive Medicine, Ministry of Health, warns rising seasonal influenza cases and outlines eight protective measures for individuals, families, and communities. Seasonal influenza is an acute respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses; transmission is mainly via respiratory droplets and contaminated surfaces. It occurs year-round but peaks during seasonal transitions with fluctuating temperatures. Most infections are mild, but severe illness and complications can occur, especially among those aged 65+, children under 5, pregnant women (particularly in the last trimester) or within two weeks postpartum, and people with chronic diseases or immunodeficiency. Measures include: wear masks in healthcare settings, on public transport, and in crowded or poorly ventilated spaces; cover mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing; frequent hand hygiene; clean commonly touched surfaces and improve ventilation; limit close contact with ill individuals; maintain a healthy lifestyle; do not self-medicate with antivirals or antibiotics; high-risk individuals should seek timely medical care.

triage.headline_ja: 保健省、季節性インフルエンザ予防・対策の8つの対策を勧告
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザに関する通常の公衆衛生啓発・予防勧告であり、異常な流行や重症例急増の報告はなく、既知の季節性疾患の範疇に留まる。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザの予防啓発記事であり、特定の流行拡大や異常事態の報告はないため対象国リストへの計上は見送った。保健省による注意喚起のみで、通常の季節的対応。

article.articleHeadline: 秋后蚊子来袭！预防"两热" 赶快消灭幼虫藏身地→
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Autumn mosquitoes are coming! Prevent "two fevers"—quickly eliminate larval habitats.
article.articleSummary: China CDC cautions in Oct 2026 that autumn is a peak period for dengue fever and chikungunya fever, with Zika virus disease also a concern, urging prevention of mosquito bites and elimination of larval habitats. Autumn temperatures of 25–30°C favor mosquito activity; surviving female mosquitoes aggressively feed to store energy for winter and drive a late-season breeding surge. Factors attracting mosquitoes include higher CO2 output, sweating/body odor, and wearing dark clothing. Prevention emphasizes removing standing water indoors and outdoors (flower pot trays, bottles, tires, bamboo tubes, tree holes). Use repellents with active ingredients like DEET (5–30%, 2–12 hours); picaridin-based products offer 4–8 hours and lower irritation. Wear light-colored long sleeves and pants in mosquito-dense areas. After bites, cold compress and calamine lotion relieve itching; seek prompt medical care if fever, rash, joint pain, or conjunctivitis develops, and report bite and travel history.

triage.headline_ja: 秋の蚊が襲来！「二つの熱病」を予防—急いで幼虫の隠れ家を駆除しよう
triage.triage_reason: 一般的な予防啓発記事であり、具体的な症例数や流行の発生を報告するものではないため、シグナルとしての基準を満たさない。
triage.notes: 本記事は中国CDCによる季節的な蚊媒介感染症（デング熱、チクングニア熱、ジカウイルス病）の一般的予防啓発であり、具体的な発生事例や症例数の報告はない。

article.articleHeadline: Malaria di Indonesia Sentuh Angka Tertinggi dalam Sejarah, Pengaruh Krisis Iklim?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria in Indonesia Reaches a Historic High, Is the Climate Crisis to Blame?
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Indonesia hits a historic high as cases rise 69% over the past two years, from 418,546 to 706,297 (2023–2025). Dengue fever is also a concern in the region. A Monash University-led Science Advances study (2026) links extreme climate change to expanded habitats for Anopheles and Aedes mosquitoes, urging stronger vector control, dengue vaccination, and greenhouse gas emission reductions to curb transmission. The research notes that climate effects are non-linear and vary by location, while globally malaria has declined over the past century even as dengue increases. In Kalimantan Timur, Kemenkes researchers are examining climate, environmental, and demographic factors in biodiverse areas to understand malaria and dengue patterns. Current measures include Wolbachia releases in Aedes and malaria control programs, with a call for coordinated, multi-pronged interventions to address both climate and non-climate drivers.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシアのマラリア、過去最高を記録 ― 気候危機の影響か？
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアでマラリア症例が過去2年で69%増加し過去最高を記録したという長期トレンドの学術的分析記事であり、突発的アウトブレイクではないため継続監視が妥当。
triage.notes: Monash大学主導の学術研究(Science Advances 2026)に基づく気候変動とマラリア・デング熱媒介蚊生息域拡大の関連性分析記事。症例数の増加トレンドは確認されるが、重症度・死亡率・緊急対応の必要性についての具体的記載はなく、既存の対策プログラム(Wolbachia放出等)で対応中とされる。

article.articleHeadline: Berlin gegen Ebola: Charité bildet 120 Klinikbeschäftigte in Afrika aus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Berlin against Ebola: Charité trains 120 hospital staff in Africa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak concentrates in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with the World Health Organization reporting over 4,000 deaths and about 1,000 active cases, and weekly spread to new regions. Uganda has 20 cases and 2 deaths; Kenya recorded its first case on October 6, with a Kenyan dying in Nairobi. The Bundibugyo subtype dominates; no officially approved standard therapy, though experimental antibody treatment and antivirals are under study. In Kinshasa, a US doctor treated with a combination therapy illustrates evolving, non-standard approaches. Charité Berlin, funded by BMZ, is training around 120 hospital staff in Africa to bolster local critical care as part of a broader response, recognizing staffing shortages and access challenges. Europe remains at low risk; France reported an imported case in June. The training aligns with the World Health Summit theme From Crisis to Resilience: Innovating for Health.

triage.headline_ja: ベルリンのエボラ対策：シャリテ病院がアフリカで120人の医療従事者を訓練
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で4000人以上の死者を出す大規模エボラ流行が継続し、ウガンダ・ケニア・フランスへの拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大な公衆衛生イベント。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国東部でのエボラ流行（Bundibugyo亜型、死者4000人超、活動症例約1000人）を中心に、ウガンダ・ケニア・フランスへの波及とドイツ（シャリテ病院）による医療従事者訓練支援を報じている。ケニア・ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: Viral Anjing Dilepasliarkan di Jagakarsa, Sudin KPKP Jaksel Beri Peringatan Keras
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rabies-Infected Dog Released in Jagakarsa; South Jakarta Department of Food Security, Maritime Affairs and Agriculture Issues Stern Warning
article.articleSummary: Rabies risk prompts stern warning as South Jakarta's Sudin KPKP (Department of Food Security, Maritime Affairs and Agriculture) addresses dog owners in Jagakarsa and Pasar Minggu after reports of around 20 dogs being released at night near Taman Spathodea. On 12 Oct, Sudin KPKP and Jagakarsa officials met with the dog owners and provided education on rules for rabies-transmitting animals (HPR); owners were urged to keep dogs confined to their yards. Officials warned that repeat incidents could lead to seizure of the animals under applicable regulations. The alert follows a social-media post describing multiple dogs being kept near a residence and concerns over injuries to neighborhood cats. No laboratory confirmation of rabies is stated in the report, but authorities emphasize rabies prevention and enforcement measures.

triage.headline_ja: ジャガカルサで犬が野放しになるとSNSで話題に、南ジャカルタ食料安全保障・海洋水産農業局（Sudin KPKP）が厳重警告
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病の検査室確認はなく、犬の野放しに関する行政指導・注意喚起の記事であり、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や異常性は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は狂犬病感染の実例報告ではなく、犬の野放しに関するSNS上の話題と行政の注意喚起・教育活動を扱ったもの。狂犬病の検査確認や症例報告はない。

article.articleHeadline: 6 dấu hiệu trẻ mắc cúm mùa cần đi khám ngay
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 6 signs your child has seasonal influenza and should see a doctor immediately.
article.articleSummary: Seasonal influenza can cause severe illness in children in Vietnam. Most present with fever and cough, but may develop rapid breathing, lethargy, poor feeding or dehydration. Six warning signs require immediate medical attention: rapid breathing with chest indrawing or blue lips; lethargy or altered responsiveness; poor intake or dehydration; prolonged high fever; fever that returns after improvement; and worsening of a preexisting condition. High-risk groups include children under 5 (especially under 2) and those with chronic lung, heart, neurological, kidney or metabolic diseases, immune suppression, cancer, chemotherapy, or long-term salicylate use. Complications include pneumonia, bacterial superinfection, respiratory failure, myocarditis, encephalitis, seizures, shock and multiorgan failure; some cases require ICU care. Vaccination is recommended annually for 6 months and older; two doses may be needed for 6–8-year-olds not fully vaccinated. Immunity develops about two weeks after vaccination; inactivated vaccines cannot cause flu. Emphasize hygiene and early antiviral therapy for high-risk cases.

triage.headline_ja: 子供が季節性インフルエンザに罹患した際、すぐに受診すべき6つの兆候
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザに関する一般的な健康啓発記事であり、特定のアウトブレイクや異常事態の報告ではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事は季節性インフルエンザの一般的な症状・重症化サインに関する保健教育コンテンツであり、特定の流行や異常発生を報告するものではない。

article.articleHeadline: लखनऊ में बारिश के बाद डेंगू ने पसारे पैर, अस्पतालों में मरीजों की कतार
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever spreads its wings after the rain in Lucknow, patients line up in hospitals.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever is spreading in Lucknow after days of heavy rain and waterlogging. As of 13 October 2026, 34 dengue patients are admitted across four major city hospitals: Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, King George’s Medical University, Balrampur Hospital, and Civil Hospital. The outbreak follows flooding and stagnant water in areas including Alambagh, Indira Nagar, Gomti Nagar, Gosai Ganj, and Chinhat, with rising Gomti River levels fueling mosquito proliferation. Health officials warn cases could rise further in the next 15 days. Preventive measures urged include removing standing water from coolers, flower pots, and tires; using mosquito nets; dressing children in full-sleeve clothing; and seeking prompt medical care for symptoms such as high fever, joint pain, and vomiting to enable dengue testing and timely treatment.

triage.headline_ja: ラクナウで降雨後にデング熱が拡大、病院に患者が列をなす
triage.triage_reason: インドの一地域（ラクナウ）での季節性デング熱流行であり、毎年繰り返される既知の現象で国際的拡大の懸念は低いが、患者数増加の可能性があるため継続観察とする。
triage.notes: 降雨・洪水後の蚊媒介増加による季節性デング熱流行で、インド国内の地方都市での公衆衛生対応事案。重症度や死亡者数に関する情報は記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: 俄研究員猝逝疑與鼠疫有關！中國留學生搶買口罩 WHO：病因未明
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russian researcher dies suddenly, suspected to be linked to plague! Chinese students studying abroad rush to buy masks; WHO: the cause of the illness is unknown.
article.articleSummary: In Irkutsk, East Siberia, a 28-year-old female researcher at an anti-plague institute died on Oct 2 after Sept 29 admission for severe pneumonia; initial symptoms resembled influenza. Russian authorities say the death stems from unknown-etiology pneumonia, not plague, with no recent plague cases in the region. Over 5,500 laboratory tests for pathogens including plague, influenza, COVID-19, and Streptococcus have been negative; all contacts completed a seven-day observation with no symptoms, and this closed Sept 9. WHO, in its Oct 10 update, found no evidence of sustained transmission but could not fully exclude laboratory exposure; no travel or trade restrictions advised. The incident prompted Chinese students in Irkutsk to stock masks, while Mongolia and China's Inner Mongolia issued health surveillance warnings. CDC assessed extremely low risk to the United States. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis; pneumonic plague spreads via droplets and is highly treatable with early antibiotics.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア人研究者が急死、ペストとの関連が疑われる！中国人留学生がマスクを買い占め；WHO：病因は不明
triage.triage_reason: 原因不明の肺炎による研究者死亡とWHO評価が示す異常性・重症性に加え、周辺国（モンゴル・中国内モンゴル）の警戒発令や中国人留学生の反応など社会的関心の高まりが確認されるため、フルRRAでの精査が望ましい。
triage.notes: 実際の発生国はロシア（イルクーツク州）であり、対象国リストに含まれない。中国（内モンゴル）やモンゴルは健康監視警告を発令したのみで、実際の感染事例発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。WHOはペストや持続的ヒト-ヒト感染の証拠はないと評価しているが、実験室曝露の可能性は完全には排除できないとしている。

article.articleHeadline: HIV Menular lewat Manikur dan Pedikur Ini Cara Mencegahnya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: HIV Transmitted Through Manicures and Pedicures: Here's How to Prevent It.
article.articleSummary: HIV transmission via manicure/pedicure tools is theoretically possible but extremely rare. A 2014 Brazilian case involved a 22-year-old woman with advanced HIV who had no sexual contact, surgeries, transfusions, tattoos, or piercings; infection was traced to sharing nail tools with an HIV-positive cousin. For transmission to occur, three conditions must align: fresh blood on a contaminated tool from someone with a high viral load, immediate reuse on another person without cleaning, and the second person having an open wound. Preventive measures include verified sterilization (UV sterilization may be non-diagnostic; request tools soaked in barbicide, effective against HIV-1, HBV, and HCV), use of stainless steel basins, technician gloves, protecting the cuticle, demanding new or properly sterilized tools, bringing personal tools, avoiding aggressive nail treatments, and promptly cleaning any hand wounds. Other realistic risks include fungal infections and hepatitis C; choosing a hygiene-forward salon remains the best defense.

triage.headline_ja: マニキュア・ペディキュアによるHIV感染：その予防方法とは
triage.triage_reason: 2014年にブラジルで報告された非常に稀な一事例を基にした一般向け予防啓発記事であり、新規の公衆衛生上の脅威や流行の兆候は示されていない。
triage.notes: 記事は2014年の過去事例を引用した一般向け健康啓発コンテンツであり、現在進行中の感染症イベントではない。ブラジルは過去事例の発生国として言及されているのみで、現行の公衆衛生イベントではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Pakar UGM Ingatkan Risiko Penularan Antraks di Balik Tradisi Brandu di Gunungkidul
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UGM Expert Warns of Anthrax Transmission Risk Behind the Brandu Tradition in Gunungkidul
article.articleSummary: Anthrax transmission risk tied to the Brandu tradition in Gunungkidul Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia. In September, four patients previously diagnosed with anthrax recovered after intensive care, while seven residents of Dusun Pelem, Kalurahan Semanu, were identified as suspects due to contact with cattle that died suddenly and were linked to meat distribution. Bacillus anthracis forms spores that can persist for decades in the environment, enabling potential recurrence. Human transmission occurs via three routes: cutaneous through skin wounds during handling or processing, inhalational via airborne spores, and gastrointestinal through ingestion of infected meat. The Brandu practice—slaughtering sick livestock and distributing cheap meat—is driven by social solidarity and economic relief (rojo koyo), but poses infection risk to communities. The Gunungkidul Health Office (Dinkes) reports four recovered cases; outreach by the Dinas Peternakan is ongoing.

triage.headline_ja: UGM専門家、グヌンキドゥルの『ブランドゥ』伝統に潜む炭疽菌感染リスクを警告
triage.triage_reason: 炭疽菌の人への感染が確認され回復例・疑い例も報告されているが、規模は限定的で国際的拡大の兆候はなく、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: 炭疽菌は風土病的に発生しており、地域保健当局が対応中。感染経路は動物由来で人-人感染はなく、継続的な食肉流通慣習（ブランドゥ）が感染源となっている点が懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Hyundai Bioscience advances Phase 2 trial of Jefti for deadly SFTS
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-13, Hyundai Bioscience announced a planned Phase 2 trial in Korea of Jefti, a niclosamide-based antiviral with drug-delivery system technology, for deadly SFTS (severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome). SFTS is tick-borne and has a cumulative domestic case fatality rate of about 18% in Korea, rising above 25% in patients aged 70+ or with underlying conditions. A Cheongju hospital incident last summer saw 7 of 9 CPR-occurring staff infected during care for a severe SFTS patient, underscoring hospital-acquired secondary infections, which comprise roughly 97% of such cases in Korea. There is no approved antiviral or vaccine; ribavirin lacks proven efficacy, and Avigan’s use yields about 15.8% mortality. Jefti reportedly shortened time to symptom improvement and lowered viral load in a COVID-19 trial; a dengue trial in Vietnam informs ongoing development. CEO Jin Geun-woo urges national support to launch domestic Phase 2 trials.

triage.headline_ja: ヒュンダイバイオサイエンス、致死的SFTS向け治療薬Jeftiの第2相試験を推進
triage.triage_reason: 記事は韓国における治療薬開発・臨床試験の企業発表であり、対象国（ベトナム等）での新規アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の異常事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 韓国（対象国リスト外）における治療薬開発の報道。ベトナムは過去のデング熱試験への言及のみで、現行のアウトブレイク情報ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: क्या है हीमोप्रोटोजोआ इंफेक्शन, जिससे कानपुर चिड़ियाघर में 4 काले हिरणों की हुई मौत? दूसरे जानवरों के लिए भी है खतरनाक
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is the hemoprotozoan infection that killed four blackbucks at Kanpur Zoo? It is dangerous for other animals as well.
article.articleSummary: Four blackbucks died at Kanpur Zoo within 15 days due to a hemoprotozoan infection. The blood protozoan illness is prompting vaccination of about 75 remaining blackbucks, with 50 vaccinated to date; the rest are slated for vaccination in the next two-three days, and vaccination of other species is planned. Officials report no further deaths since vaccination began, suggesting protection in effect. Indian Veterinary Research Institute scientists say the infection spreads via blood-sucking flies from one animal to another, underscoring the need for preventive vaccination. The zoo’s director, Dr. Kanhaiya Patel, says the disease poses a risk to other animals and a prioritized vaccination plan is being implemented to curb the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: カンプール動物園のブラックバック4頭死亡、原因の血液原虫感染症とは？他の動物にも危険
triage.triage_reason: 動物園内の野生動物（ブラックバック）の血液原虫感染症であり、人への感染性やヒト公衆衛生への影響は報告されていない。ワクチン接種で対応済みで、拡大リスクも限定的。

article.articleHeadline: [현장] 현대바이오 "살인진드기 치료제 개발에 전력... 뎅기열 범용제
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: [On-site] Hyundai Bio: "Devoting all its efforts to developing a treatment for the killer tick... a universal dengue fever drug."
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-13, Hyundai BioScience announced at the Korea Press Center the launch of Phase 2 clinical development for Jefti (Xafty), a universal broad-spectrum antiviral targeting dengue fever and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), diseases with no approved therapies. Hyundai says Phase 2 in Korea will address urgent domestic needs, with an emphasis on the SFTS season (April–November). Jefti has shown SFTS antiviral activity in preclinical work; recent independent animal studies reported 100% survival at defined drug exposure, enabling accelerated trials. The company plans rapid Phase 2 progression for SFTS after consultations with the MFDS, drawing on safety data from COVID-19 trials. Vietnamese health officials attended; dengue trials in Vietnam are progressing in Phase 2/3. The briefing referenced Japan’s 2024 conditional approval of a dengue drug despite not meeting Phase 3 endpoints as a precedent.

triage.headline_ja: 【現場】ヒュンダイバイオ「殺人ダニ治療薬開発に全力…デング熱汎用薬」
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は製薬企業による治療薬開発（臨床試験）の発表であり、実際の感染症アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急事態を報じるものではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事は治療薬（Jefti/Xafty）の臨床開発に関する企業発表であり、ベトナムでの言及は臨床試験進捗の文脈であって、疾病発生そのものの報告ではないため、発生国として確定できない。韓国・日本は対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue battle goes aerial as Punjab deploys drones to spray larvicide in Patiala hotspots - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-13, Punjab launches aerial dengue control in Patiala under a 60-Day Emergency Vector Control Cycle (Phase-I), deploying drones to spray larvicide in hotspots and hard-to-reach breeding pockets. A MoU between the Department of Health and Family Welfare and Kiran Corporation/SPV enables drone-based larval control, with daily field reporting and surveillance of larval and adult mosquitoes to monitor outcomes. The initiative targets source reduction, complementing the Har Shukarvar Dengue Te Vaar campaign and prior door-to-door larvae surveillance that reportedly reduced cases and yielded zero dengue deaths this year. Patiala recorded a high disease burden in 2025. The operation is non-financial for the state; a review within 10 days of completion will assess larval-density reductions and guide scale-up to other districts.

article.articleHeadline: Pemprov Papua targetkan Biak dan Supiori capai eliminasi malaria 2029
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Papua Provincial Government targets Biak and Supiori to achieve malaria elimination by 2029.
article.articleSummary: Papua Province aims for malaria elimination in Biak Numfor and Supiori by 2029 as malaria transmission remains narrowly confined in these districts. In Biak Numfor, malaria-positive cases are found in 20 of 24 villages, while in Supiori transmission is confined to four villages, according to Silas Mabui of the Papua Health Office. Achieving elimination implies zero sustained locally acquired cases, with ongoing measures required to prevent rebound. Major challenges include patients' adherence to complete antimalarial treatment; many stop after the first day. Vector control is emphasized through proper use of malaria bed nets and environmental sanitation, including clearing home surroundings, proper waste disposal, and draining standing water to reduce mosquito breeding. The effort underscores continuous surveillance and case management to maintain a zero-case status and reach the 2029 target.

triage.headline_ja: パプア州政府、ビアクとスピオリでのマラリア排除を2029年までに達成することを目標
triage.triage_reason: 既知の風土病であるマラリアの排除計画に関する行政広報記事であり、異常性や急激な公衆衛生上の脅威は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシア・パプア州における既存のマラリア流行地域での排除目標達成に向けた取り組みを報じるもので、新規発生や異常な増加を示すものではない。Papua New Guineaは発生地域に含まれるが記事主題ではなく対象国リストにも該当しないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: [현장] 치료제 없는 '살인 진드기병'...현대바이오가 나섰다
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: [On the Scene] A deadly tick-borne disease with no treatment... Hyundai Bio has stepped in.
article.articleSummary: Hyundai BioScience (South Korea) plans a domestically conducted Phase 2 trial of Jefti (XAFTY), a broad‑spectrum antiviral whose active ingredient is niclosamide, for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), a tick‑borne viral disease. SFTS starts with flu‑like symptoms and can progress to organ failure, with about 200 Korean patients affected annually and a ~20% fatality rate; last year, one in seven Korean patients died. Jefti targets host pathways, aiming to curb multiple viruses and reduce resistance. Hyundai seeks MFDS pre‑consultation and submission of the clinical plan, aiming to dose patients by early May next year. SFTS currently has no approved treatments; Japan approved Favipiravir (Avigan) for SFTS after small trials. Globally, Hyundai’s US unit joined the MCDC; trials are ongoing in Vietnam for dengue and in the US for other indications, reflecting broad development of Jefti.

triage.headline_ja: 【現場】治療薬のない「殺人ダニ病」…現代バイオが乗り出す
triage.triage_reason: 既知のSFTSに対する治療薬（Jefti）の臨床試験計画に関する企業ニュースであり、新規感染症の発生や拡大を報告するものではないため。
triage.notes: 記事は韓国企業Hyundai BioScienceによるSFTS治療薬Jeftiの臨床試験計画（韓国国内）を主題とする企業・医薬開発ニュース。ベトナムでのデング熱治験言及はあるが、現地での感染症発生報告ではなく治験実施の文脈のため対象国として計上せず。

article.articleHeadline: Mor: černá smrt a její tažení Evropou a místa spojená s morovými epidemiemi v Česku - Kudy z nudy
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Plague: the Black Death and its spread across Europe and places associated with plague epidemics in the Czech Republic - Kudy z nudy
article.articleSummary: Yersinia pestis, the Black Death, devastated Europe from the 14th to the 18th centuries, killing an estimated one-third to one-half of its population. In the Czech lands, its memory survives in ossuaries and plague columns: Sedlec Ossuary near Kutná Hora; the Mělník church ossuary; Brno’s Church of St. James ossuary; Kolín’s ossuary; and Prague’s Olšany cemetery, begun after 1679 as a plague burial ground. Notable memorials include Brno’s Morový sloup on náměstí Svobody, and Marian plague columns in Olomouc, Kutná Hora, Bakov nad Jizerou, Velvary, Moravská Třebová, and at Hradčanské náměstí in Prague; chapels such as St. Rocha near Zlaté Hory (1632) and Kalvárie at Jaroměřice u Jevíčka. The former plague hospital U nuzných in České Budějovice (1371; rebuilt ~1515) later became a poorhouse. Transmission includes pneumonic and bubonic forms; today Europe is largely free, though Madagascar, Congo, and Peru remain active foci.

triage.headline_ja: ペスト：黒死病とそのヨーロッパ全土への拡大、およびチェコにおけるペスト流行関連史跡
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は歴史的・観光的な黒死病に関する解説記事であり、現在進行中の感染症イベントを報告するものではない。DRC等の現存流行地への言及はあるが具体的な発生報告ではないため見送り。
triage.notes: 記事は歴史・観光情報が主題であり、現在のアウトブレイクに関する新規情報は含まれていない。DRC、マダガスカル、ペルーが現存の流行地として言及されているが、具体的な事例報告ではないため対象国にも含めない。

article.articleHeadline: 俄研究員猝逝疑與鼠疫有關！陸生搶買口罩
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A Russian researcher dies suddenly, suspected to be linked to plague! Mainland Chinese students scramble to buy masks.
article.articleSummary: In Irkutsk, eastern Siberia, a 28-year-old female researcher at an anti-plague institute died on Oct 2 after Sept 29 admission for severe pneumonia. Russian authorities say the death is due to pneumonia of unknown etiology, not plague, and there is no evidence of ongoing plague transmission; more than 5,500 tests, including for plague, influenza, COVID-19, and Streptococcus, were negative. The patient had been vaccinated against high-threat pathogens and had not left Irkutsk region in two weeks prior to onset; two independent investigations found no laboratory biosafety incidents. Close contacts were hospitalized or observed at home for seven days; none developed symptoms. WHO notes no evidence of sustained transmission but cannot completely rule out laboratory exposure and urges further testing and strengthened respiratory-disease surveillance. US CDC regards the risk to the United States as extremely low. Chinese students at Irkutsk National University reportedly stockpiled masks; Mongolia border health monitoring and Inner Mongolia plague risk alerts were issued.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア人研究員が急死、ペスト関連の疑い！中国人留学生がマスクを買い占め
triage.triage_reason: ペスト研究所勤務の研究者が原因不明の重症肺炎で死亡し、WHOが実験室曝露の可能性を完全には否定できないとして注視を呼びかけており、モンゴル国境監視や内モンゴルでの警戒発令など渡航関連の対応も見られるため、異常性と国際的注目度からフルリスク評価が妥当と判断した。
triage.notes: 事例発生地はロシア・イルクーツク州であり、対象国リストに含まれない。中国（内モンゴル）は予防的な警戒発令・マスク買い占めの報道のみで、実際の症例発生は確認されていないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Pemkab Jayawijaya targetkan eliminasi malaria pada 2027
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Jayawijaya Regency Government Targets Malaria Elimination by 2027.
article.articleSummary: Malaria elimination targeted by 2027 in Jayawijaya Regency, Papua Highlands, Indonesia. Plt Head of the Jayawijaya Health Office, Esau R. Aibesa, in Wamena outlined steps including capacity-building training for physicians at RSUD and local health centers (puskesmas) to ensure rapid, accurate malaria management. The plan emphasizes strengthening health facilities, proactive case detection, and community prevention measures. Most malaria cases are imported; local transmission is currently very low. No severe malaria cases or deaths have been reported; existing cases are outpatient and manageable at health facilities. Preventive actions promoted include the use of bed nets, environmental cleanliness, draining standing water, clearing tall grasses, and keeping homes mosquito-free. The initiative prioritizes training and socialization to achieve elimination by 2027.

triage.headline_ja: ジャヤウィジャヤ県政府、2027年までのマラリア撲滅を目標に設定
